Bulk or politically motivated attempts to delete voters from rolls may become harder.
Genuine voters may face fewer wrongful deletion challenges, though enforcement details remain to be seen.

reports.headline: Amid bulk filing, ECI sets limit on Form 7 submissions
reports.summary: Applications during claims and objections that an individual elector can file are capped at 10, while those during continuous updation of rolls by a voter have been fixed at five per month

events.headline: Census 2027: Ensure every individual is counted, says Registrar General
events.why: Census 2027 is a nationwide exercise whose accuracy and timeliness shape data used for planning public services across India.
implications: Households may be visited by enumerators and asked to provide accurate details in the second phase.
Complete counts could improve how welfare schemes and public services are planned.
Missed deadlines or undercounting may delay the release of national census data.

reports.headline: Census 2027: Ensure every individual is counted, says Registrar General
reports.summary: Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan asks census officials in Andhra Pradesh to complete the second phase with accuracy and within deadlines

events.headline: Centre moves to bar retailers, wholesalers from advertising prescription drugs
events.why: Proposed national rules to stop retailers and wholesalers advertising prescription drugs would tighten medicine marketing regulation.
implications: Consumers may see fewer promotions nudging them toward prescription-only medicines.
Chemists and wholesalers could need to change their advertising practices once the rules are notified.

reports.headline: Centre moves to bar retailers, wholesalers from advertising prescription drugs
reports.summary: The Centre has invited public feedback on the proposed rules within 30 days for final notification.

events.headline: Rural roads: Centre enlists IIT, NIT academicians for quality checks, fixing defects
events.why: Independent academic inspections of India's roughly 800,000-km rural road network could improve the quality of a major public infrastructure programme.
implications: Villagers may get more durable roads with fewer defects and repeated repairs.
Contractors may face tighter accountability, and poor work could more often be flagged and corrected.

reports.headline: Rural roads: Centre enlists IIT, NIT academicians for quality checks, fixing defects
reports.summary: The ministry of rural development is bringing in IIT and NIT academicians for inter-state inspections to pinpoint defect causes and boost accountability across India’s 800,000-km rural road network.

events.headline: India overhauls medical device safety rules, expands digital surveillance
events.why: Revised national safety rules widen oversight of medical devices, including AI-enabled tools, and extend reporting down to primary health centres.
implications: Device makers may face tighter reporting and cybersecurity compliance duties for software and AI-enabled products.
Primary health centres could need to report device faults and adverse events, adding to their workload.
Patients may gain better safeguards against faulty or insecure medical devices over time.

reports.headline: India overhauls medical device safety rules, expands digital surveillance
reports.summary: New guidelines widen monitoring of AI-enabled devices, software glitches and cybersecurity risks while extending reporting to primary health centres.

events.headline: FSSAI send notices to Dr Reddy's, Nestle Health Science, Amazon, Flipkart over misleading protein supplement
events.why: The national food regulator is acting against misleading health claims by major brands and e-commerce platforms, signalling tighter oversight of the fast-growing supplement market.
implications: Protein and health supplement makers may need to revise labels and advertising claims to comply with FSSAI rules.
Consumers could see fewer exaggerated health claims on supplements sold online and in stores.
E-commerce platforms may face more responsibility for vetting the food and health products they list.

reports.headline: FSSAI send notices to Dr Reddy's, Nestle Health Science, Amazon, Flipkart over misleading protein supplement
reports.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has sent notices to companies, including Dr Reddy's and Nestle Health Science, regarding products which can possibly mislead consumers regarding its health benefits. It issued notices for non-compliant advertising and misleading claims.

events.headline: 72 lakh teachers trained to use technology to identify students with disabilities
events.why: A nationwide digital screening drive using 72 lakh teachers could widen early identification of disabilities and access to inclusive education.
implications: More children with disabilities may be identified early and referred to special educators.
Teachers may take on added screening duties this month using the digital tool.
Identified students could become eligible for support services under 21 disability categories.

reports.headline: 72 lakh teachers trained to use technology to identify students with disabilities
reports.summary: Teachers to use a digital screening tool this month to spot observable behaviours; special educators will then categorise students under 21 disability categories; early detection and intervention to aid inclusive education

events.headline: Government notifies CAPF Act amid pending challenge in Supreme Court
events.why: The notified CAPF Act changes how senior posts and cadres are managed in central forces, despite a pending Supreme Court challenge.
implications: Cadre management in the Central Armed Police Forces may change, affecting promotions of serving officers.
IPS deputation to senior CAPF posts will be shaped by the new law.
The Supreme Court challenge could alter or delay how the Act is applied.

reports.headline: Government notifies CAPF Act amid pending challenge in Supreme Court
reports.summary: Serving CAPF officers have challenged the law, which will impact cadre management and the deputation of Indian Police Service officers to senior positions in the Central Armed Police Forces

events.headline: Centre plans 30% trade-margin cap on non-scheduled cancer drugs
events.why: A national cap on trade margins for non-scheduled cancer drugs targets steep mark-ups and could sharply lower the cost of cancer treatment.
implications: Retail prices of some cancer medicines could fall by up to 70% if the cap is implemented.
Patients and families facing long-term cancer treatment may see lower out-of-pocket spending.
Distributors and retailers of these drugs may face thinner margins.

reports.headline: Centre plans 30% trade-margin cap on non-scheduled cancer drugs
reports.summary: The proposed cap could cut retail prices by up to 70%, with the government moving ahead of a broader crackdown on steep mark-ups in cancer medicines.

events.headline: NAAC’s new accreditation framework to prioritise outcomes over inputs
events.why: NAAC's shift to outcome-based accreditation could change how higher education institutions across India are assessed and ranked.
implications: Colleges and universities may need to show patents and skilled graduates rather than just documents.
Institutions may shift focus toward skills and employability, which could affect students' course quality.
Accreditation-linked funding and recognition could depend more on measurable results.

reports.headline: NAAC’s new accreditation framework to prioritise outcomes over inputs
reports.summary: Institutions will have to demonstrate tangible outcomes, such as commercially relevant patents and the number of skilled students produced, rather than merely furnishing documents

events.headline: SC directs Centre to form expert panel to regulate unethical pharma marketing
events.why: A Supreme Court direction to form an expert panel could lead to stronger rules on pharmaceutical marketing practices nationwide.
implications: Doctors' prescribing may face tighter scrutiny over gifts and incentives from drug makers.
Patients could see fewer influenced prescriptions and possibly lower medicine costs over time.
Pharma firms may need to change how they market to doctors.

reports.headline: SC directs Centre to form expert panel to regulate unethical pharma marketing
reports.summary: The petition had raised concerns over pharmaceutical companies allegedly offering doctors expensive gifts, overseas trips, and other incentives to encourage the prescription of particular drugs

events.headline: Supreme Court moves to tighten rules on pharma freebies to doctors
events.why: A Supreme Court push for a panel on pharma gifts to doctors could lead to enforceable rules on drug promotion nationwide.
implications: Doctors' prescribing practices may face tighter scrutiny if binding rules are introduced.
Drugmakers could have to change promotional spending, which may affect medicine pricing over time.

reports.headline: Supreme Court moves to tighten rules on pharma freebies to doctors
reports.summary: The top court has asked the Centre to set up a three-member panel to examine whether drugmakers need legally enforceable rules governing gifts, incentives and other promotional practices.

events.headline: Bengaluru CJP protest today: Prakash Raj, Dhruv Rathee to join ‘people’s tribunal’ in SIR protest | Key things to know
events.why: Protests over the electoral roll revision (SIR) raise questions on electoral transparency and voter inclusion nationwide.
implications: Citizens may face closer verification of their voter registration during the roll revision.
Scrutiny of the Election Commission's process could intensify ahead of the planned October 10 demonstration.

reports.headline: Bengaluru CJP protest today: Prakash Raj, Dhruv Rathee to join ‘people’s tribunal’ in SIR protest | Key things to know
reports.summary: Bengaluru's Freedom Park will host a CJP protest against electoral roll revisions, featuring activists and public figures. The protest precedes a planned demonstration on October 10.

reports.headline: 'Zero transparency, zero accountability from EC', alleges YouTuber Dhruv Rathee addressing SIR protest in Bengaluru
reports.summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee accused the Election Commission of lacking transparency and accountability over the SIR exercise at a protest in Bengaluru. Actor-activist Prakash Raj called for the exercise to be scrapped, saying it threatened citizens’ rights and dignity.

events.headline: State, UT-level Bankers’ Committees asked to report share of SC beneficiaries in jobs, loan subsidy schemes
events.why: A national advisory requires bankers' committees to report SC beneficiary data, improving oversight of inclusive access to bank credit and subsidies.
implications: Banks may have to collect and report SC beneficiary data in job and loan subsidy schemes.
Better data could help regulators spot gaps in credit access for SC borrowers.
Monitoring of state-level lending performance by the National Commission for SCs may improve.

reports.headline: State, UT-level Bankers’ Committees asked to report share of SC beneficiaries in jobs, loan subsidy schemes
reports.summary: Finance Ministry directs SLBCs/UTLBCs to report share of SC beneficiaries in flagship schemes to aid NCSC monitoring and inclusion aims.

reports.headline: Why have SLBCs/UTLBCs been asked to report SC beneficiary data for key government schemes for jobs and entrepreneurship? | Explained
reports.summary: The primary focus of the SLBS is supposed to be on “policy and strategic issues relating to the flow of priority sector credit and overall financial inclusion in the state”, as per the RBI guidelines governing the functioning of the committees

events.headline: CEC appointment law row: SC to examine plea seeking recall of September split verdict
events.why: The Supreme Court's handling of the CEC appointment law row affects how India's top election officials are chosen and how much trust voters place in them.
implications: A recall hearing could reopen the legal basis for the current appointment process for election commissioners.
The outcome may shape how elections are overseen and how credible they are seen to be.

reports.headline: CEC appointment law row: SC to examine plea seeking recall of September split verdict
reports.summary: On Wednesday, a bench comprising the Chief Justice of India and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan.

events.headline: ECI Row: What happens when all three Election Commissioners disagree? Here's what the law says
events.why: Public disagreement inside the Election Commission raises questions about how India's poll body would function if its three members cannot agree, which bears on electoral credibility.
implications: Clarity on the legal position may shape confidence in how upcoming electoral roll revisions and elections are run.
Prolonged internal splits could delay or complicate decisions on poll schedules and roll updates.
The row may prompt calls for rule changes on how the Election Commission decides contested matters.

reports.headline: ECI Row: What happens when all three Election Commissioners disagree? Here's what the law says
reports.summary: What happens when all three Election Commissioners disagree? As the ECI faces scrutiny over internal differences, here’s what the law says if the poll panel is stuck in a 1-1-1 split.

reports.headline: SIR row: Supreme Court refuses to pass interim order on suspending CEC Gyanesh Kumar, issues notices to EC, Centre
reports.summary: Plea in SC to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar: A Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant issued notice to the Election Commission of India, seeking its response on the allegations made in the plea.

reports.headline: Supreme Court notice to ECI, Centre on plea challenging decisions taken by CEC-led poll panel
reports.summary: Supreme Court seeks responses from ECI and Centre after petitions alleging unilateral CEC-led decisions and immunity concerns in India’s election governance.

reports.headline: SC declines to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar, seeks response on poll body decisions
reports.summary: The Supreme Court bench said the modified Form 6, which is used for inclusion of names in the electoral list during the process of SIR, was not approved by the court.

reports.headline: Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar LIVE: Supreme Court says changes to Form 6 not made by court, issues notice to ECI, Centre
reports.summary: Follow The Hindu Live for further updates as protests continue against CEC Gyanesh Kumar as the Supreme Court hears pleas challenging his decisions and seeking his suspension from office.

reports.headline: ECI fact-checks claims on Form 6 following SC observation
reports.summary: ECI and PIB fact-check claims about Form 6 changes, CJI remarks, and Rahul Gandhi’s allegations amid Bihar SIR uproar.

reports.headline: CEC Gyanesh Kumar has lost public trust and must be removed, say former bureaucrats, activists
reports.summary: Group of retired officials and activists demand removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of six misbehaviours and blocking access to the ECI.

reports.headline: Key developments in the ECI row: A timeline
reports.summary: Protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified over the last week, with several detained, and complaints of sexual harassment against ACP Vivek Bhagat in Delhi.

reports.headline: CJI agrees to take a call on hearing a plea to recall split verdict in CEC appointments law case
reports.summary: SC agrees to hear recall plea over split verdict on CEC appointments law, amid allegations of judicial bias disclosure.

reports.headline: CEC row LIVE: SC to examine plea for recall of split verdict on law governing appointment of CEC, ECs
reports.summary: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi were released after being detained during the INDIA bloc’s protest march towards Jantar Mantar.

events.headline: Meet Justices Sunita Agarwal, DK Upadhyay, Aparesh Singh: Centre notifies appointment of 3 judges to Supreme Court
events.why: Elevating three High Court Chief Justices brings the Supreme Court to 37 of 38 judges, supporting the functioning of the country's apex judiciary.
implications: Near-full strength may help the Supreme Court handle its large pending caseload more steadily.
Litigants and businesses awaiting apex court hearings could see modestly faster listing of cases.

reports.headline: Meet Justices Sunita Agarwal, DK Upadhyay, Aparesh Singh: Centre notifies appointment of 3 judges to Supreme Court
reports.summary: The Centre appointed three High Court Chief Justices as Supreme Court judges: Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice DK Upadhyay, and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh. This follows a recommendation from the Supreme Court Collegium. The Supreme Court now has 37 judges, one short of its sanctioned strength of 38.

reports.headline: Centre elevates three Chief Justices to Supreme Court
reports.summary: Centre elevates three Chief Justices from Gujarat, Delhi, and Telangana High Courts to the Supreme Court, boosting strength to 37.

reports.headline: CJI Surya Kant administers oath to three new judges, judges count now 37 in Supreme Court
reports.summary: Three new judges sworn in by CJI Surya Kant, raising Supreme Court strength to 37 of 38 sanctioned seats.

events.headline: Panel on simultaneous elections Bills meets media personalities and economists
events.why: The parliamentary panel's consultations on the simultaneous elections Bills are part of a major proposed change to India's electoral system.
implications: The consultation outcome could shape the final form of the Bills and the timeline for synchronised polls.
If passed, the changes could alter how often states and the Centre hold elections and the related costs.

reports.headline: Panel on simultaneous elections Bills meets media personalities and economists
reports.summary: Parliament panel weighing simultaneous elections heard media and economists, sparking objections over Sudhir Chaudhary’s witness inclusion and hybrid viewpoints.

reports.headline: DMK MP defends the simultaneous polls panel’s plan to meet CJI
reports.summary: DMK MP defends panel's study tour on simultaneous polls, arguing informal judicial views are constitutional and separation of powers allows dialogue.

events.headline: GST arrest powers may be removed? Council to discuss decriminalisation on Wednesday; law change likely in Winter Session
events.why: Removing GST arrest powers would change how tax law is enforced against businesses across India and ease compliance fears.
implications: Traders and small businesses may face less fear of arrest during GST investigations and disputes.
Any change would likely need a law amendment, possibly in the Winter Session.
Tax officials may have to rely more on penalties and recovery than arrests.

reports.headline: GST arrest powers may be removed? Council to discuss decriminalisation on Wednesday; law change likely in Winter Session
reports.summary: GST enforcement could see a major shift as the Centre and states weigh changes to arrest powers under the indirect tax regime. The proposal comes amid concerns over how these provisions have been used against businesses. Here’s what could change and what it means.

reports.headline: GST Council meeting postponed for second time, rescheduled to October 8
reports.summary: The 57th GST Council meeting has been postponed again and will now be held on October 8, instead of October 7. The meeting will discuss changes to GST registration, returns, and refund mechanisms.

reports.headline: GST Council meeting rescheduled for Thursday, says official order
reports.summary: The GST Council meeting has been rescheduled to Thursday in New Delhi. The meeting will focus on process reforms and compliance simplification rather than rate changes.

events.headline: Health groups seek regulation of private hospital charges, medicine margins
events.why: Calls for uniform regulation of private hospital charges and medicine margins raise a national health-pricing policy question affecting patients across India.
implications: Ceilings on hospital charges could lower out-of-pocket bills for patients if authorities act on the demand.
Capping trade margins on medicines may reduce drug prices for households.
Private hospitals may resist, so any change could take time to arrive.

reports.headline: Health groups seek regulation of private hospital charges, medicine margins
reports.summary: Groups urge ceilings on private hospital charges and trade margins for medicines, devices, and consumables, plus accessible patient grievance mechanisms.

events.headline: Aadhaar name correction new rules 2026: Which document do you need for spelling mistake, marriage or major name change?
events.why: Revised UIDAI rules set document requirements for Aadhaar name changes, affecting the identity system that underpins banking, subsidies and public services nationwide.
implications: Residents correcting names after marriage or spelling errors will need specific prescribed documents for each type of request.
Applicants submitting affidavits or Gazette notifications may face stricter UIDAI verification, which could slow some updates.
Mismatched names could be cleared more reliably, easing access to bank accounts, KYC and welfare benefits.

reports.headline: Aadhaar name correction new rules 2026: Which document do you need for spelling mistake, marriage or major name change?
reports.summary: Under the revised rules, Aadhaar holders have to submit the prescribed supporting documents for their particular request. UIDAI will verify the authenticity of documents, affidavits and Gazette notifications submitted for the update.

events.headline: Mint Explainer | Why Karnataka’s gig worker law has put platforms and workers at odds
events.why: The dispute tests whether states can run their own gig worker social-security regimes alongside a national law, shaping the federal approach to platform labour.
implications: Gig workers may face different social-security rules and contributions depending on the state they work in.
Platforms operating nationwide could face varying compliance costs and levies across states.
Clarity from courts or the Centre may be needed to settle which law prevails.

reports.headline: Mint Explainer | Why Karnataka’s gig worker law has put platforms and workers at odds
reports.summary: At the heart of the dispute is a question: can states create their own social-security regimes for gig workers when Parliament has already enacted a national law covering them?

events.headline: IndiaTech seeks rethink of turnover-linked gig worker social security levy
events.why: The turnover-linked social security levy under the Code on Social Security will shape costs for platforms and protection for gig workers nationwide.
implications: Platform aggregators may face higher compliance costs if the 1-2% turnover levy is applied as written.
Delivery and ride-hailing workers could gain social security cover once contributions are finalised.
Any rethink of the levy could change how quickly gig worker benefits arrive.

reports.headline: IndiaTech seeks rethink of turnover-linked gig worker social security levy
reports.summary: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, aggregators are required to contribute 1-2% of annual turnover towards social security for gig and platform workers, subject to a cap of 5% of the amount paid or payable to such workers.
